A1.justification: Both readable PDFs describe the same LAPI study, with matching methods, experiments and figures. v1 references but does not include Appendices A–C; v2 supplies Appendices A–D. These additions can be assessed as newly supplied documentation without assuming corresponding procedural changes.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original ophthalmology Q&A experiments, numerical comparisons in Table 1, component ablations in Table 2 and a response case study.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds GPT-4 comparisons with enhanced chain-of-thought variants in Appendix D, Table 3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, line 6 changes random response selection from all generated responses S to the all-rules-satisfied category Call. This localized algorithm correction aligns the pseudocode with v1's existing prose and diagram; HBM planning and entropy-based prompt refinement remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate ophthalmology patient-question answering using the same hospital dataset. The added CoT comparison introduces no new dataset, population or task. Other professional domains are discussed only as unvalidated applications.

E2.justification: Appendix D adds three evaluated GPT-4 comparators: CoT-(P.R.), CoT-(HBM) and CoT-(HBM+P.R.). These extend the existing CoT baseline with pragmatic rules, HBM guidance or both. Table 1 retains its original comparator membership.

E3.justification: The reported main settings remain 400 Q&A pairs, 300 retrieval pairs, 10 test inquiries, five base models and the same metrics and sampling parameters. Appendix B supplies previously missing evaluation details. Lower-is-better ROUGE-L precision already appears in both Table 1 captions, so the corrected prose does not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a targeted analysis asking whether LAPI's advantage persists when CoT receives HBM guidance and pragmatic rules. The existing HBM/entropy ablations in Table 2 and the laser-surgery response case study are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The unchanged five-response sampling parameter and pragmatic entropy concern the method, rather than newly added uncertainty reporting for experimental results.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises GPT-3.5 LAPI naturalness from 3.45 to 3.60, patient-centricity from 3.55 to 3.70 and recall from 0.30 to 0.29, matching the unchanged Table 2 row. Table 3 adds scores for three enhanced CoT variants. Other shared numerical results and case-study responses are unchanged.

T1.justification: The satisfaction-rate and pragmatic-entropy definitions remain mathematically unchanged. Notation is simplified and the redundant response-regeneration equation is removed, while its operation remains in the algorithm. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: professional identity through HBM-guided planning and pragmatic entropy, with improved medical-response quality. The additional CoT comparisons support these existing claims rather than redefine their scope.

C2.justification: New Section 7 acknowledges reliance on LLM judgments, the need for clinical validation, limited generalizability from the small sample and unvalidated transfer beyond medical Q&A. Section 5.1 also changes the interpretation of ROUGE-L precision to lower-is-more-informative, matching the existing table caption.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C supply the previously absent initial-prompt template, GPT-4 evaluator identification, detailed 1–4 scoring rubrics, and five pragmatic rules with their derivation. Section 8 newly reports anonymization, verbal consent and hospital IRB approval. These substantially expand documentation without establishing that the underlying settings changed.

R1.justification: Appendix C adds five medical-communication references supporting the pragmatic rules, including Allen et al., Chen et al. and Zhang et al. The broader research positioning remains stable. Numerous author, year and bibliography corrections concern already cited works rather than new literature.

P1.justification: Sections 4.3 and 5.4 receive localized condensation and rewriting. v2 adds limitations, ethics, acknowledgements and appendix sections, plus a corresponding-author designation. Most existing prose and the ordering of Sections 1–6 remain intact.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted with different page geometry, larger body text, narrower columns and revised citation styling. Figure 2 is redrawn; v1's Figure 3 moves to Appendix A as Figure 4; Figure 5 and Table 3 are added. The case-study figure is retained with a shorter caption.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through the supplied prompts, rules, scoring rubrics and ethics disclosures. It also corrects the selection pseudocode and cross-table inconsistency, adds closer CoT controls and acknowledges limitations. These are useful gains, but the central evidence remains a small, LLM-judged study, and claims of superiority on every ablation metric still conflict with Table 2.
